newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Glaxo falls after stg dents profits.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Glaxo falls after stg dents profits.

text.p: Shares in British drug giant Glaxo Wellcome Plc fell back on Thursday after the strong pound dented first-half profits and sales.

Pre-tax profit fell by 2.2 percent to 1.517 billion pounds ($2.5 billion), while sales slipped 1.9 percent to 4.109 billion stg. The dividend was left unchanged at 15.0 pence as Glaxo rebalances its interim and full-year payouts.

The world's second-biggest maker of prescription drugs said its strategy to manage the decline of top-selling anti-ulcerant Zantac and herpes treatment Zovirax was firmly on course, with sales of a package of new products including asthma treatment Serevent jumping by 50 percent.
"The new products are powering ahead and driving the growth, and that is what we always said. Zantac is disappearing from view," chairman and chief executive Sir Richard Sykes told Reuters.

But some analysts detected the first sign of jitters over the imminent demise of the two blockbusters, both off patent in the all-important U.S. market, which will keep Glaxo's sales and profits flat at best until the end of 1998.

Glaxo shares slipped 3.1 percent or 41 pence to 1288-1/2 pence after the company said the strong pound and spending on the launch of a clutch of replacement products would cut profit margins to around 35 percent of sales this year.
"Anybody who has got Glaxo shares has got to be assuming that the market is prepared to live with that miserable outlook," said Dresdner Kleinwort Benson analyst Peter McDougall.

But Alyson Coates of SocGen added "it is nothing to do with the next 12 months, it is where you think it is going afterwards. If you think it is one of the best drug companies in the world then it is extremely cheap."
Glaxo said the strong pound had wiped about ten percent off first-half profits and sales, and predicted an eight percent hit for the full-year.
Stripping out moves in exchange rates, Glaxo said underlying sales were up by eight percent. Ignoring Zantac, sales were ahead by 14 percent, putting it up with the best of its U.S. rivals.
Sales of Zantac fell 20 percent to 807 million pounds, reflecting generic competition in markets including Britain and Germany and the continued advance of rival products like Astra AB's Losec.

Although competition in the US has been delayed by squabbles among generic producers, Sykes said he still expected copycat versions to wipe out up to 90 percent of Glaxo's U.S. sales, which totalled around 400 million pounds in the first half.

Respiratory drugs, which include Serevent and Flixotide, overtook Zantac for the first time to become the biggest-selling category, with sales up an underlying seven percent to 891 million pounds. Other star performers included AIDS treatment Epivir and migraine drug Imigran.

A new diabetes drug Romozin, which won its first European marketing approval in Britain on Wednesday, a powerful anti-biotic Raxar and a novel anti-smoking tablet Zyban are all due for launch in the second half of the year, Glaxo Wellcome said. ($ = 0.612 British Pounds)
